201:| `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Canonical base64 of exactly 32 cryptographically random bytes for AES-256-GCM; identical across instances. A placeholder/password is invalid. Key loss prevents decryption; rotation/migration is not implemented. |
214:State and browser secrets use 32 random bytes each. Five-minute state records contain only hashes, role and expiry. The state is consumed atomically with a matching browser hash; valid denial/code-error callbacks consume it too. Replay, expiry, cookie duplication, wrong browser, duplicate query parameters, wrong role/account, and unknown callback parameters fail closed. The browser cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/; HTTPS uses Secure and the `__Host-` prefix. It is cleared after callback. Starting another flow in the same browser replaces the cookie; complete one connection at a time.
234:`!mark word` or `!mark emoji` submits a mark through the already authenticated `channel.chat.message` boundary. Inputs receive Unicode NFKC, locale-independent lowercase and explicit sharp-S/final-sigma folding. The bounded conservative policy accepts one letters/combining-marks word or one supported emoji grapheme (including ZWJ families, modifiers, flags and keycaps). It rejects spaces, control/bidi/invisible word characters, HTML/link syntax and a small substring blocklist. Input is capped at 128 UTF-8 bytes and 32 normalized code points. The filter is intentionally conservative, can reject benign text, and is not comprehensive multilingual abuse/confusable moderation; moderator approval is still required.
256:**Hard storage bounds:** each channel document retains at most 16 explicit stream sessions, at most **32 participants per active stream**, at most **five marks per participant / 160 marks per stream**, and at most **160 retained mark records across all sessions**. Participant slots remain consumed for the active stream after forgetting, so content erasure cannot defeat the cap. Two block lists are capped at 128 numeric IDs each, and cross-stream cooldown entries at 128. IDs/text are length-bounded, with a **128 KiB serialized-document guard** on every mutation, well below Firestore's 1 MiB limit. At mark/participant capacity, submissions are acknowledged without mutation; session/block/document capacity errors fail closed. Retention cleanup and archival expansion are pending; a 17th retained session requires a reviewed retention policy. This per-channel ledger trades throughput for simple prototype atomicity. Event dedupe documents and public output never contain actor identities or pending mark text.
